title: Real Numbers: Rational and Irrational Numbers, Roots and Rounding
seo_title: Grade 9 Real Numbers Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Describe the real number system by recognising, defining and distinguishing properties of natural numbers, whole numbers, integers, rational numbers and irrational numbers; recognise and use rounding off and estimation.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 9 real numbers worksheets: rational and irrational numbers, recurring decimals, estimating roots and significant figures. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Rational: can be written as a fraction.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A rational number can be written as a fraction ab: terminating and recurring decimals are rational.
  • An irrational number cannot: √2, √7 and π never end or repeat.
  • √50 is between 7 and 8 because 49 < 50 < 64.
  • Significant figures start at the first non-zero digit: 0,004 07 has 3 significant figures.

Examples

Example

Is √0,25 rational?

√0,25 = 0,5

Answer: yes, rational

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Every decimal is irrational0,333… is rational.
√16 irrational√16 = 4.
Leading zerosThey are not significant.

items.e: −7 can be written as a fraction, so it is rational.
